chunks: From him, from Al-Hakam Al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The female singer who escorts the brides, there is no objection to her earnings."

key_terms.تَزُفُّ: She escorts/leads (specifically in a wedding procession)

ai.seo_question: Is the income of a female wedding singer permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that the specific profession of a female singer accompanying brides (*tazuff*) yields permissible (*halal*) earnings, distinguishing it from general singing which may be subject to debate. This hadith highlights the Shia juristic focus on the context and function of the act rather than the act itself, affirming the legitimacy of cultural expressions in celebratory contexts. It serves as a key precedent in the chapter of earnings (*al-Makasib*) for validating income derived from artistic performance when not inherently linked to prohibited elements like illicit gatherings or obscenity.
